query: What pension reform was adopted and what risks to the pension system remain?
answer: The 2025 pension reform created a Single Solidarity Fund—capitalized by merging the reserves of the legacy DB and mixed schemes and backed by an annual $966 million government transfer (which will increase annually by up to 4 percent)—to finance current and future benefits across all schemes. It also established a non-contributory solidarity pension component to improve the social safety net, obliged self-employed workers to participate with a 9.36 percent contribution of taxable income, and raised employer contribution rates from 4.25 percent to 7.25 percent in three one-point steps in 2025, 2027, and 2029 (while employee contributions remain at 9.25 percent). Additionally, flexible investment rules were introduced. Regarding risks and remaining challenges, the IMF staff notes that future parametric adjustments will be needed to ensure long-term sustainability, as part of the assets of the mixed scheme will now be used to pay pensions of the DB scheme. Further adjustments, such as reassessing and raising the currently low retirement age (at 57 for women and 62 for men), will be needed. Meanwhile, the authorities expect the reform to secure roughly 15 years of positive cash flows, encourage participation and formal employment, and boost asset returns through flexible investment rules.
